q.t: Fill in: I like tea ___ coffee. (both)
q.e: Adding one to the other → and.

q.t: Fill in: She is poor ___ honest.
q.e: A contrast (poor, yet honest) → but.

q.t: Fill in: Would you like rice ___ chapati?
q.e: A choice → or.

q.t: Fill in: It was raining, ___ we stayed indoors.
q.e: The rain caused us to stay in → so (result).

q.t: Fill in: He was absent ___ he was ill.
q.e: Being ill is the reason → because.

q.t: Fill in: Wait here ___ I come back.
q.e: Up to the time I come → until.

q.t: Choose the interjection that shows pain.
q.e: ‘Ouch!’ is what we say when something hurts.

q.t: Choose the interjection that shows joy.
q.e: ‘Hurray!’ shows joy or celebration.

q.t: Fill in: ___! We have won the match.
q.e: Winning makes us happy → Hurray.

q.t: Find the conjunction: I called him but he did not answer.
q.e: ‘but’ joins the two parts and shows the contrast.

q.t: Fill in: ___ it was cold, she went out without a coat.
q.e: A surprising contrast (cold, yet no coat) → Although.

q.t: Fill in: ___ you work hard, you will not pass.
q.e: ‘Unless’ = if not: If you do not work hard, you will not pass.

q.t: Fill in: He is ___ clever ___ hard-working.
q.e: Two qualities added together → both … and.

q.t: Fill in: ___ Ravi ___ Mohan was at home. (neither of them)
q.e: Not one and not the other → neither … nor.

q.t: Fill in: You can ___ stay ___ leave.
q.e: One of two choices → either … or.

q.t: Fill in: I will call you ___ I reach home.
q.e: Time: immediately after I reach → as soon as.

q.t: Fill in: He saved money ___ he could buy a bicycle.
q.e: Purpose → so that.

q.t: Choose the interjection for sorrow: ___! The poor dog died.
q.e: ‘Alas!’ shows sorrow.

q.t: Choose the interjection for praise: ___! You played well.
q.e: ‘Bravo!’ shows approval.

q.t: Join: She was tired. She finished the work.
o: Though she was tired, she finished the work.
She was tired, so she finished the work.
Because she was tired, she finished the work.
She was tired or she finished the work.
q.e: Finishing despite being tired is a contrast → though.

q.t: Find the error: Although he is rich, but he is not happy.
q.e: ‘Although’ already shows the contrast; adding ‘but’ doubles it.

q.t: Find the error: Unless you do not hurry, you will miss the train.
q.e: ‘Unless’ already means ‘if not’, so a second ‘not’ reverses the meaning.

q.t: Fill in: No sooner had he left ___ it began to rain.
q.e: ‘No sooner’ always pairs with ‘than’.

q.t: Fill in: Hardly had I sat down ___ the doorbell rang.
q.e: ‘Hardly / Scarcely’ pair with ‘when’.

q.t: Fill in: The box was ___ heavy ___ I could not lift it.
q.e: ‘so + adjective + that’ shows result. (‘too … to’ would need ‘too heavy for me to lift’.)

q.t: Fill in: It was ___ a hot day ___ we stayed indoors.
q.e: ‘such + a + adjective + noun + that’.

q.t: Choose the correctly balanced sentence.
o: He plays not only the piano but also the guitar.
He not only plays the piano but also the guitar.
Not only he plays the piano but also the guitar.
He plays not only the piano but the guitar also too.
q.e: Put each half right before matching words: ‘the piano’ and ‘the guitar’ are both nouns.

q.t: Fill in: I don't know ___ he will come or not.
q.e: ‘whether … or not’ shows two possibilities.

q.t: Fill in: Walk carefully ___ you should fall.
q.e: ‘lest’ = so that … not. It is followed by ‘should’.

q.t: Fill in: He doesn't eat meat, ___ does he eat eggs.
q.e: Adding a second negative → nor (followed by the question-style order: does he).

q.t: Join: He worked hard. He failed. (show contrast in one simple clause)
o: In spite of working hard, he failed.
In spite of he worked hard, he failed.
Despite of working hard, he failed.
Although working hard he failed but.
q.e: ‘In spite of’ (or ‘Despite’, never ‘despite of’) is followed by a noun or -ing form, not a full clause.

q.t: Join using ‘no sooner’: The thief saw the police. He ran away.
o: No sooner did the thief see the police than he ran away.
No sooner the thief saw the police than he ran away.
No sooner did the thief see the police when he ran away.
No sooner did the thief saw the police than he ran away.
q.e: ‘No sooner’ + did + subject + V1 … than. ‘did’ carries the past, so ‘see’ is V1.

q.t: Fill in: Take an umbrella in case it ___.
q.e: Like ‘if’ and ‘unless’, ‘in case’ takes the simple present for a future idea.

q.t: Which sentence uses since as a conjunction of REASON?
o: Since you are busy, I will come later.
I have lived in this house since 2010.
It has been raining since early morning.
I haven't seen him since last summer.
q.e: Here ‘since’ = because. In the others it shows time.

q.t: Which sentence uses as to show TIME?
o: As I was leaving, the phone rang.
As he was ill, he stayed home.
She is as tall as me.
q.e: ‘As I was leaving’ = while I was leaving.

q.t: Fill in: Rina is tall, ___ her brother is short. (comparing two facts)
q.e: ‘whereas’ compares two contrasting facts.

q.t: Find the error: Neither the teacher or the students were present.
q.e: ‘Neither’ pairs with ‘nor’. (‘were’ is right — it agrees with the nearer ‘students’.)

q.t: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
q.e: The interjection stands outside the sentence’s grammar, so a comma (or !) separates it.

q.t: Join: You must leave now. Otherwise you will be late.
o: You must leave now, or you will be late.
You must leave now and you will be late.
You must leave now, so you will be late.
You must leave now because you will be late.
q.e: ‘otherwise’ = ‘or else’ → or.

q.t: Fill in: She speaks ___ she knew everything.
q.e: ‘as if’ shows manner — the way she speaks, imagining something that may not be true.
